description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace" to store intermediate results and ensure it is empty before use.
2. Produce a complete recursive listing of all entries under /working and save that listing to "temp_workspace/listing.txt".
3. From "listing.txt", extract all entries whose final pathname component equals "workspace" and save those paths to "temp_workspace/candidates.txt".
4. For every path in "candidates.txt", obtain and record its file-type metadata (e.g., regular file, directory, symlink) into "temp_workspace/metadata.txt".
5. Normalize the candidate paths in "temp_workspace/candidates.txt" to absolute form and remove duplicates, saving the result to "temp_workspace/candidates_clean.txt".
6. Using "metadata.txt" and "candidates_clean.txt", determine for each candidate whether it is a regular file and write those determinations to "temp_workspace/verification.txt".
7. If any entry in "verification.txt" is marked as a regular file, create an empty marker file "temp_workspace/found_regular.flag"; otherwise ensure that marker file does not exist.
8. Read the presence or absence of "temp_workspace/found_regular.flag" and prepare the final decision so that it can produce "yes" if present or "no" if absent, without emitting that decision yet.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Create a temporary workspace folder named "temp_workspace" to hold intermediate artifacts.  
2. Obtain a complete recursive listing of all entries under /working and save it to "temp_workspace/raw_listing.txt".  
3. From "temp_workspace/raw_listing.txt", extract and save only entries that represent regular files to "temp_workspace/files_list.txt".  
4. Filter "temp_workspace/files_list.txt" for entries whose name is exactly "workspace" and write those paths to "temp_workspace/candidate_paths.txt".  
5. For each path in "temp_workspace/candidate_paths.txt", verify the path currently exists and is a regular file, recording positive verifications to "temp_workspace/verified_candidates.txt".  
6. Remove duplicate paths from "temp_workspace/verified_candidates.txt" and save the unique results to "temp_workspace/unique_verified.txt".  
7. Count the number of lines in "temp_workspace/unique_verified.txt" and save that integer to "temp_workspace/match_count.txt".  
8. Prepare a concise summary file "temp_workspace/final_ready.txt" that references "temp_workspace/unique_verified.txt" and includes the value from "temp_workspace/match_count.txt", making the verification results ready for the final decision step.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace" to hold all intermediate artifacts and recordings.  
2. Obtain a recursive inventory of every filesystem entry under /working and save that inventory to "temp_workspace/listings.txt".  
3. Extract from the inventory every path whose final component is exactly "workspace" and write those paths to "temp_workspace/candidates.txt".  
4. For each path listed in "temp_workspace/candidates.txt", retrieve and record its filesystem metadata (including type) into "temp_workspace/metadata.txt".  
5. From the recorded metadata, filter and retain only entries identified as regular files, saving the results to "temp_workspace/regular_candidates.txt".  
6. Confirm each retained regular candidate resides within the /working subtree, remove duplicate paths, and write the deduplicated list to "temp_workspace/unique_regular.txt".  
7. Append a timestamped audit summary to "temp_workspace/audit.txt" stating the count of entries in "temp_workspace/unique_regular.txt" and verify all intermediate files are readable.  
8. Create a readiness marker file named "temp_workspace/ready_for_decision" indicating that all preparation artifacts are complete and the set is ready for the final yes/no determination.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_check" to hold all intermediate files and results.  
2. Recursively enumerate every filesystem entry under /working and save the full paths to "temp_workspace_check/all_paths.txt".  
3. From that list, extract entries whose filename exactly matches "workspace" and save those paths to "temp_workspace_check/candidate_paths.txt".  
4. For each candidate path, determine whether it is a regular file and append regular-file paths to "temp_workspace_check/verified_paths.txt" and non-regular matches to "temp_workspace_check/nonregular_paths.txt".  
5. Record key attributes (file size and modification time) for each verified path into "temp_workspace_check/attributes.txt" alongside the path.  
6. Re-check the attributes for each verified path and compare them to the recorded attributes, writing any discrepancies to "temp_workspace_check/consistency_issues.txt" and consistent entries to "temp_workspace_check/consistent_paths.txt".  
7. Remove or archive intermediate lists that are no longer needed (specifically "all_paths.txt" and "candidate_paths.txt") while keeping the verified and consistency files and ensuring the temporary folder is readable for follow-up steps.  
8. Create a single summary file "temp_workspace_check/decision_ready.txt" that contains the count of consistent verified paths and the list of those paths, prepared for the final determination.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
